meta.title: {name}: add it to Chrome
meta.description: TwoTicks is a free panel for WhatsApp Web with a privacy screen, unanswered chats, quick replies, a scheduler and more. Add it to Google Chrome from the Chrome Web Store in four steps.
nav.label: Sections
hero.note: Free, with no account. For Google Chrome {minChrome} or newer on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS.
store.name: Chrome Web Store
install.title: Install in four steps
install.intro: TwoTicks is in the {store}. Chrome adds it with a click and keeps it up to date by itself.
install.allDone: All ticks are blue: TwoTicks is installed.
step1.title: Open TwoTicks in the {store}

step4.title: Open WhatsApp Web

faq.title: Questions and answers
faq.privacy.q: Does TwoTicks read or send my chats?
faq.update.q: How does TwoTicks get new versions?
faq.update.a: Chrome updates it by itself from the {store}, usually within a few hours of a new version. Your settings, quick replies and scheduled messages stay as they are.
faq.browsers.q: Which browsers and computers does TwoTicks run on?
faq.browsers.a: Google Chrome {minChrome} or newer on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Chrome on phones and tablets has no extensions. Other browsers built on Chromium, such as Microsoft Edge, can often add extensions from the {store} as well, but TwoTicks is made and tested for Google Chrome.
faq.mcp.q: Can AI programs on my computer use TwoTicks?
faq.mcp.a: Yes, with TwoTicks MCP, a free and optional program for Windows: AI programs such as Claude Code can then use TwoTicks' tools, and whatever sends or changes something waits for your confirmation. {link}
faq.blocked.q: Chrome does not let me add TwoTicks
faq.blocked.a: If the button in the store is greyed out, or Chrome says that your administrator has blocked the extension, an organisation manages this Chrome. Ask whoever manages the computer.
faq.remove.a: Right-click the TwoTicks icon in Chrome's toolbar and choose {removeFromChrome}. You can also open {address} and click {remove} on the TwoTicks card.
tool.how: Open WhatsApp Web, click the dark button with the two ticks or press {keys}, and choose {panelTool} in the panel's list of tools.

mcp.metaTitle: TwoTicks MCP: TwoTicks' tools in Claude Code and other AI programs
mcp.description: A free, optional program for Windows that lets AI programs on your computer, such as Claude Code, use the tools of TwoTicks for WhatsApp Web. Whatever sends or changes something waits for your confirmation.
mcp.lead: An optional extra for people who work with AI programs. With the free TwoTicks MCP program, an AI program on your computer, such as Claude Code or VS Code, can use TwoTicks' tools: it looks at unanswered chats, summarises, analyses attachments and prepares messages, which go out only after your confirmation.
mcp.ctaSetup: Set it up, step by step
mcp.facts: Free and optional, for Windows 10 and 11. TwoTicks works fully without it.

mcp.term.q2: Were you able to send the documents?

mcp.term.p1.title: You ask in your own words
mcp.term.p1.text: Claude Code picks TwoTicks' tools itself: unanswered chats, summaries, attachments, scheduling.
mcp.term.p2.title: You confirm every message
mcp.term.p2.text: You see who gets what. In the confirmation window you can correct the text, and when several messages wait together you can leave single ones out.
mcp.term.p3.title: TwoTicks sends nothing to the internet
mcp.term.p3.text: TwoTicks MCP opens no network port either. What a tool returns goes to your AI program, which usually sends it on to the company that runs its AI model.

mcp.flow1: You ask it in your own words, for example in Claude Code.
mcp.flow2.name: TwoTicks MCP
mcp.flow2: It passes the request on to TwoTicks in Chrome, on your computer only.

mcp.need1: Windows 10 or 11, and Google Chrome with TwoTicks {version} or newer from the {store}.
mcp.need3: An AI program that supports MCP (the Model Context Protocol), for example Claude Code, or VS Code with GitHub Copilot.
mcp.stepsTitle: Set it up in three steps
mcp.step1.title: Install TwoTicks MCP
mcp.step1.text: Open the Command Prompt: press the Windows key, type cmd and press Enter. Paste this command and press Enter:
mcp.step1.after: The command copies the program into your user folder and registers it with Chrome for your Windows user only, without administrator rights; Chrome lets only TwoTicks start it. Where Claude Code and VS Code are installed, it adds the server “twoticks” to them.
mcp.step1.ps: In PowerShell, type {npxcmd} instead of {npx} if Windows says that running scripts is disabled.
mcp.step1.npx: On its first run npx asks before it downloads the package ({ask}): type {y} and press Enter.
mcp.step1.opens: When it has finished, the command opens TwoTicks' settings in Chrome on the tab {tab} and waits there for the connection.
mcp.step2.title: Agree in TwoTicks
mcp.step2.text: On the page that has opened, read what the connection means and click {agree}. Chrome then asks once for a new permission, {permission}: click {allowChrome}. About half a minute later, the page and the Command Prompt both say that TwoTicks is connected. If no page opened, open TwoTicks' settings and the tab {tab} yourself.
mcp.step3.title: Ask in your own words
mcp.step3.text: Start your AI program, or open a new session if it was open, and ask. For example:
mcp.step3.other: Claude Code and VS Code, which the install command sets up itself, are allowed with your agreement. Every other AI program, also one whose model runs on your own computer, is asked about when it connects for the first time: click {allow} in TwoTicks' settings or in the window it shows on WhatsApp Web. Allow only programs that you started yourself.
mcp.ask1: Which chats are waiting for my answer?
mcp.ask2: Summarise what was said in the family group this week.
mcp.ask3: Look at the PDF my accountant sent me and list the dates in it.
mcp.ask4: Write a short reply to my landlord and send it once I have read it.
mcp.cc.title: If you use Claude Code
mcp.cc.p1.title: The install command adds it
mcp.cc.p1.text: The install command adds the server “twoticks” to Claude Code for all your projects: to Claude Code in the terminal and to the Claude Code extension in VS Code alike. There is nothing else to type.
mcp.cc.p2.title: Open a new session
mcp.cc.p2.text: Claude Code loads its tools when a session starts: after installing, start Claude Code again or open a new session. Once it is connected, TwoTicks' settings show it as {now}; in Claude Code in the terminal, the command {mcp} lists “twoticks” too.
mcp.cc.p3.title: Claude Code asks as well
mcp.cc.p3.text: Before it uses one of TwoTicks' tools, Claude Code asks you itself; if you allow a tool for good there, it does not ask about that tool again. TwoTicks' confirmation is separate: whatever sends, schedules, deletes, changes or exports something still waits for your confirmation.
mcp.cc.p4.title: In VS Code, you confirm on WhatsApp Web
mcp.cc.p4.text: Claude Code's panel in VS Code does not show confirmation forms for now. TwoTicks then asks for your confirmation in its window on WhatsApp Web: switch to WhatsApp Web in Chrome and confirm there.
mcp.cc.p5.title: If it says {notFound}
mcp.cc.p5.text: If the install command did not find Claude Code, run it once more after installing Claude Code. If it still does not find it, run the {add} line that it prints, in the Command Prompt.
mcp.toolsTitle: What your AI program can do
mcp.toolsIntro: TwoTicks decides which tools there are, and you switch their groups on and off in its settings. Tools marked {tag} act only after your click.
mcp.offByDefault: Off until you switch it on.
mcp.confirm1: Before anything is sent, scheduled, deleted, changed or exported, you see exactly what will happen, and nothing happens without your click: in your AI program where it can ask you itself, otherwise in TwoTicks' own window on WhatsApp Web. With {confirmHere} switched on in the settings, TwoTicks always asks on WhatsApp Web.
mcp.confirm2: TwoTicks' limits stay: 15 to 60 seconds between two messages and at most 30 messages in 24 hours. Before a message goes to several chats, you confirm that everyone on the list has agreed to receive messages from you.
mcp.confirm3: View-once photos and videos are never passed on, and neither are chats in which someone switched on WhatsApp's Advanced chat privacy.
mcp.confirm4: In that confirmation you can correct a message’s text before it goes, and when several messages wait together you can leave single ones out.
mcp.confirm5: A file from your computer is shown to you before it goes: the picture itself, a player for a sound, and for a PDF or Word document its name, its folder and its first lines.
mcp.files1: Photos, PDF, Word and Excel files, voice messages and videos from your chats reach your AI program as files. TwoTicks MCP saves them in a folder {folder} inside the project your AI program works in, or else in Documents › TwoTicks MCP. The folder gets a .gitignore file, so attachments do not end up in git by mistake.
mcp.files2: TwoTicks reads the text of PDF, Word and Excel files on your computer. Voice messages are written down by Chrome's built-in model where Chrome has one; otherwise your AI program gets the recording as a file. You need no API key for any of this: your AI program does the thinking.
mcp.files3: Each saved file is marked as coming from the internet, as a download in the browser is, and programs are never saved.
mcp.privacy1: TwoTicks and TwoTicks MCP send nothing to the internet. What a tool returns goes to your AI program, which usually sends it on to the company that runs its AI model, under that company's terms. Chats contain other people's words, names and voices: pass on only what you may.
mcp.privacy2: TwoTicks MCP opens no network port. Chrome starts it only for TwoTicks, and its two parts talk through a Windows named pipe that answers only programs with a key from your own user folder.
mcp.privacy3: Each AI program has to be allowed once in TwoTicks. TwoTicks keeps a log of which program used which tool, never of what it read or sent.
